text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert P1 - INF-RUNTIME-23: runtime-eu-west1 serving pool reporting OOMs -> elevated 502/503 errors for customer-facing generation endpoints. Pager triggered at 1763000000.
maya: I'm oncall — looking now. I see repeated `cudaMalloc` failures from runtime-agent logs and ~4 tenants reporting timeouts.
maya: quick mitigation — I'm applying a per-pod cap: set `max_batch_size=1` on runtime-eu-west1 canary (3 pods) to avoid concurrent peak allocations, and will restart the worst offending pods.
sam: copy. any immediate customer-facing rollback or fallback planned?
maya: enabling fallback to smaller model (redwood-3b) for tiered customers as a temporary policy. pushing canary config now.
alex: sharing a recent log snippet from the runtime side: 
```text
[2026-02-12T14:22:11Z] runtime: allocation failed: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
pid=2345 model=redwood-13b vram_used=22500MB vram_total=24576MB
GPU0: free 1200MB, reserved fragments: [512MB, 256MB, 256MB] fragmentation_ratio=0.42
```
maya: also grabbed a quick `nvidia-smi` snapshot from the affected host: 
```text
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| NVIDIA-SMI 510.73       Driver Version: 510.73       CUDA Version: 11.6     |
| GPU  Name        Persistence-M| Bus-Id        Disp.A | Volatile Uncorr. ECC |
| 0    A100 40GB      On           00000000:17:00.0  On | 0                 |
| 0  40960MiB / 40960MiB | 98%                                     |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```
lina: hypothesis: this looks like memory fragmentation (lots of small reserved chunks) compounded by long KV cache retention for conversational sessions. Small free holes can't satisfy large contiguous allocs -> cudaMalloc fails even though aggregate free memory exists.
maya: I dug into workload traces — sequence lengths increased for a few customers after a product change yesterday (sticky context). KV cache per-request growth correlates with the timeframe.
sam: what was the OOM rate before/after the intervention? numbers?
maya: before mitigation: ~12 OOMs/min across cluster and ~6% 503s for eu customers. After setting `max_batch_size=1` and restarting 3 pods + forcing KV eviction on those pods: OOMs dropped to 0-1/min and 503s dropped to 0.8%.
ops-bot: runtime-scaling: increased node pool by +2 GPUs in eu-west1 (provisioning).
alex: here's the `pmap` memory map from a leaking process (sanitized): 
```text
0x7f8a3e000000-0x7f8a3e400000 rw-s 00000000 00:05 123456 /dev/nvmap
0x7f8a3e400000-0x7f8a6000000 rw-s 00000000 00:05 234567 /dev/nvmap
heap: total 22.1GB, mmaped fragments ~1.3GB spread across many small regions
```
lina: another hypothesis: the allocator (custom GPU allocator) doesn't compact across freed small allocations; repeated small KV inserts/evicts over long sessions leave fragmentation. When a big attention scratch allocation requests contiguous pages, it fails.
sam: temporary mitigations observed to help: 1) lower batch sizes, 2) force full KV eviction between requests for high-length sessions, 3) periodic pod restarts to reclaim fragmented VRAM. Are we doing any aggressive compaction in runtime?
maya: not currently. There is a compaction flag but it's disabled due to latency risk. We tested enabling `gpu_compact=true` on canary pods — initial run shows ~30% reduction in fragmentation ratio but adds ~40ms median extra latency on first token.
alex: we did a controlled restart of 3 pods and forced KV eviction:
```bash
kubectl exec runtime-pod-47 -- curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/evict_kv_cache
kubectl rollout restart deploy/runtime-eu-west1 -n prod --field-selector metadata.name=runtime-pod-47
```
maya: immediate effect after restart + eviction: `fragmentation_ratio` reported by agent dropped from 0.42 -> 0.18 on those hosts. OOMs fell off.
ops-bot: Incident notes: affected tenants: tenant-a, tenant-c, tenant-d, tenant-e. Fallback to smaller models active for tenant-a and tenant-d.
sam: are we confident this was fragmentation + KV growth, not an unrelated leak? any evidence of steadily increasing resident set size?
alex: RSS per-process did not trend steadily upwards for the processes we sampled; instead memory was reallocated into small mmap regions, consistent with fragmentation rather than a continuous leak.
lina: action items I'm proposing:
- short term: keep `max_batch_size=1` for eu-west1 for 2h, scheduled pod restarts every 4h for 24h for the most loaded hosts.
- medium: enable `gpu_compact` behind a feature flag with metrics and a canary rollout.
- long term: allocator work to support defragmentation without big latency cliffs, and add per-tenant KV eviction heuristics based on session length.
maya: I'm handing this off to sam for the post-incident timeline & RCA write-up. I'll stay on as advisory.
sam: got it. I'll compile timeline + attach logs and GPU stats to the RCA ticket ENG-7894.
maya: working note for timeline:
- 14:22:00 pager triggered (OOM spikes)
- 14:23:10 mitigation: `max_batch_size=1` canary + restart 3 pods
- 14:24:40 fallback policy enabled for big tenants (3b model)
- 14:26:05 OOM rate dropped below alert threshold
- 14:30:00 node-pool +2 GPUs requested
- 14:45:00 monitoring shows stable error rate
sam: I'll also question product for yesterday's sticky context change (could be root cause trigger) and add an eval to simulate long-session KV churn.
lina: please gather `cuda_mem_info` dumps, `pmap` outputs, and runtime-agent diagnostics into the RCA thread. I'll start a short doc with hypothesis table (fragmentation vs leak vs bad allocator behavior).
maya: customer impact summary for SOC: roughly 10-15 min degraded performance for affected tenants, tail error rate up to 6% during spike, mitigated within ~8 minutes of initial intervention.
ops-bot: Reminder: create postmortem in /incidents/rca and link ENG-7894.
maya: logging action: I'll upload the sanitized logs to the RCA doc and ping infra for allocator tracing.
sam: thanks all — moving to post-incident channel next. If it flares again, page me directly and I'll take immediate control.
